name: Ultimate V60 Technique (Hario USA transcription)
author: James Hoffmann
agitation: swirl in bloom; stir once each way after last pour; gentle swirl before drawdown
notes: Ratio inferred. Temperature only as hotter is better; rinse filter with water just off the boil. Drawdown target 3:30.

name: Ultimate V60 (18 g gist)
author: James Hoffmann (transcribed by fluency03)
agitation: swirl in bloom; stir once each way after last pour; gentle swirl before drawdown
notes: Pour times differ from the Hario USA schedule (0:45 and 1:15 there). The fetch may have mis-ordered the steps. Bloom at most 3x dose.

name: A Better 1 Cup V60 Technique
author: James Hoffmann
grind: medium-fine (one summary says finer for light roasts)
agitation: swirl at 5 s after bloom and about 2:00 after last pour
notes: Third-party transcription; another summary gives about 2:30 total. Designed for plastic 01 V60. Temperature 100 C per aeroprecipe; another summary says freshly boiled.

name: Scott Rao V60 recipe
author: Scott Rao
agitation: aggressive spin in bloom; very gentle spin (under 1 s) after pours 1 and 2
notes: Published 2022-05-10. Plastic V60. Pour 3 is after about 70% drawdown, not a fixed time. Extraction yield stated as 22-24.5% (depends on grinder, varietal, roast).

name: 4:6 Method (Hario Europe)
author: Tetsu Kasuya
agitation: not stated
notes: First 40% of water (pours 1-2) sets acidity vs sweetness: more water in pour 1 = more acidity. Last 60% sets strength. WBC table lists 3:00 total; Long Short London gives 92-95 C and 3:30 total; Kurasu transcription gives different pour times.

name: Pour Over Masterclass V60 Technique
author: Lance Hedrick (as presented by LAMOSE)
agitation: 3-5 gentle stirs in bloom; gentle swirl after each pour; spiral pours 3-4 inches above bed
notes: Retailer page, not Hedrick's own site. Drawdown target 2:45-3:00: slower than 3:15 means grind coarser, faster than 2:30 means finer. Water TDS target 75-150 ppm.

name: Matt Perger V60
author: Matt Perger
agitation: thorough stir in bloom; lift and tap brewer after pouring
notes: Dose unreadable in the PDF table (a g/L column shows 58, which would imply about 11.6 g for 200 g; do not use). Original Barista Hustle source not found.
